routes.notes: The homepage on the playbook's homepage board: one city's cityPlans read model in one of three states, with how a night works, the proof, organisers, the host band, the app band and the FAQ. Busy: five or more plans in the next 14 days, with format chips. Thin: an open city with fewer than five, which lists every plan with its date and moves the host band up to third. Launching: the hero leads with hosts and the opening-day notice sits where the plans would be. A city whose plans cannot be read stays busy and says so, never "New" or a count. Review state ids are unchanged: thin-city and launching-soon are the thin and launching states, mumbai-live the busy one.

Website v2 Explore (CAT-261): a city's plans and organisers from its cityPlans read model, with search, format and date filters in the URL. City pages such as /mumbai/ are its linkable city state (canonical to themselves; cities not yet open are noindex until CAT-181). The organisers view is where /organizers/ redirects.

Every city the website lists, by country and status, from contracts/catalogs/markets.json and each city's cityPlans read model. An open city links its city page with its honest count; a city not open links the homepage launch notice (/?city=slug#whats-on). A country with no city open says "Launching soon in {country}" once. The footer's More cities link and the header picker lead here.

The host landing, band for band as the RbWebHostV2 board on the system: hero, kinds of night, a night on Catch (chapters), the iPad, the applicant board (replay), guests, growth links, layers, pricing (slider), FAQ and the free-trial start band, whose store badges begin the trial in the app. The retired-route anchors sit on the bands that carry their content. The site header names the product and its sections.

No-download Event Success runtime. The opaque public id resolves only bounded event metadata; Firebase phone OTP binds the attendee to an imported roster row or a Host approval request before event-scoped profile and live tools unlock.

Scoped event-service update and approved guest replies. The URL fragment supplies a private bearer credential; the route does not unlock attendance, assignments or a roster. Marketing analytics are excluded.

Anonymous, synthetic-only guest phone for a Host dress rehearsal. A high-entropy link redeems one deterministic browser slot without OTP, follows the Host virtual clock, and never reads or writes the live event domain.

Opaque invitation resolver for private or public operational events. It records a deduplicated open, then sends a Catch event's invitation to its event page with the token as il, and an external or event-mode invitation to its issued destination, without adding the event to public discovery. Booking happens on the event page (CAT-252).

Private household RSVP surface for organizer programs. The signed path token scopes reads and writes to one household's invited functions; messaging consent is an explicit checkbox, never implied by a positive RSVP.

A household's weekend (RbProgItinerary): the functions they said yes or maybe to, by day, the journeys they sent, where they stay, Add to calendar and Change our reply. Reads the household RSVP view by the household's signed path token. Private token link: noindex, out of the sitemap, no analytics.

The household's IDs for the hotel (RbProgIdGuest): each member with Added or Add (getProgramGuestIdStatus, names and status only), and one member's kind of ID with front and back photos, uploaded through createProgramAssetUpload's signed POST and saved with submitProgramGuestId. Private token link: noindex, out of the sitemap, no analytics.

The hotel front desk's rooming list with ID status (RbProgHotelHandover, 1280) by a hotelHandover link: four figures, the rooms table with accepted ID photos signed for minutes, Download the rooming list (CSV made in the browser) and the privacy notice. Private token link: noindex, out of the sitemap, no analytics.

A driver's trip (RbProgDriver) by a driverTrip link: trip, car and plate, pickup and drop, passengers with party sizes and bags, Directions by place names. No phone numbers or flights in the read. Private token link: noindex, out of the sitemap, no analytics.

A vendor's view-only run sheet (RbProgRunSheet) by a vendorRunSheet link: the programme's functions by day marked done, now, next and later, and a car vendor's trips. No guest names or contacts in the read. Private token link: noindex, out of the sitemap, no analytics.

The porters' welcome hampers (RbProgHampers) by a hamperPorter link: rooms done over a meter, a row per room with Done or Placed, the photos, and Placed · take a photo, saved through upsertProgramHamper with a signed photo upload. Room labels and guest counts only. Private token link: noindex, out of the sitemap, no analytics.

The family's view-only counts (RbHostProgramShare) by a family link: the spotlight in the programme's colour, guests and households replied, who is coming to each function, heads for the caterer and how many households have still to reply, read through getProgramFamilyView. Counts and function names only. Private token link: noindex, out of the sitemap, no analytics.
No-download, opaque-link organizer form route with version-bound autosaved drafts, configurable identity verification, review, idempotent submission, withdrawal, and source attribution.

Redirects to Explore's organisers view (CAT-261): the Next route answers 308 to /explore/?show=organisers with the original query, and the static build redirects in the browser. Organiser pages under /organizers/<slug>/ are unchanged. Stays noindex until CAT-181 decides when the directory becomes indexable.
Claim landing route with static noindex output. Firebase Hosting serves nested claim lookup URLs through /claim/index.html.

Structured listing request form (takedown plan, section 7): step 1 a fixed request type (claim, correct a fact, remove and don't list again, trademark, copyright, privacy, impersonation, court or government order), step 2 that type's fixed fields with the target prefilled from ?organizer= or ?event= when opened from a listing, step 3 the fixed declarations, then the reference and what happens next. Posts to /api/listing-request (submitListingRequest). Noindex, out of the sitemap, disallowed in robots.txt, and no analytics.

DRAFT Listing Policy for counsel review: what Catch lists, sources, not-affiliated labels and how to claim or remove. Unlinked, noindex and out of the sitemap, with the draft banner, until counsel approves.

DRAFT Notice and Takedown Policy with the Grievance Officer section (details from the brand config) for counsel review: the request types, channel, verification, timelines, counter-notice, appeal and repeat abuse. Unlinked, noindex and out of the sitemap, with the draft banner, until counsel approves.
Client lookup variant parsed by getClaimListingLookupFromLocation; Firebase Hosting rewrites /claim/** to the static /claim/index.html shell.
Published privacy policy with confirmed operator, contact, grievance, data-use, rights, retention, safety, and public-source listing terms.
Published terms for the website-first pilot, external events, public-source listings, accounts, conduct, safety, and governing law.
Published account, privacy, listing, event, safety, website, correction, claim, and takedown support route.
Canonical store-listing account deletion resource: in-app deletion for Catch and Catch Host, the no-app email request path, and what is deleted versus retained.

Published refund and cancellation policy for paid Catch event tickets: organiser as seller, the Flexible, Standard and Strict cash refund deadlines enforced by checkout, organiser cancellation, waitlists, and refund timing.
Published operator contact page: Torana operating Catch, postal address, support email, phone and WhatsApp, and the grievance officer.
Unknown direct routes are served through the generated root 404.html with HTTP 404; client-side unknown routes render the same noindex not-found page.

Generated canonical organizer profile routes from website/src/generated/hostListings.json. The deployable projection includes only organizers with at least one market whose status is live in the active market pack; waitlist-market records remain available to review tooling and Storybook but cannot enter static output, search, or sitemap. Postbuild emits crawlable semantic profile content, Organization JSON-LD, canonical metadata, and lastVerifiedAt sitemap dates before React starts. Consumer profile presentation shares the homepage navigation and visual system. Community identity and follow/share lead into events, about, reviews, and source/ownership context. Preserve authenticated follows, review provenance and permissions, external booking links, and empty event states. Catch Experience is an explicit event-level participation declaration, never an organiser endorsement.
Generated legacy organizer routes must preserve canonical URL and noindex after hydration.

Generated Event Detail routes for explicitly published Catch events and public imported events, rendered from the eventPublicPage read model (CAT-250, CAT-252), or from the organizer listing under the same publication rules until a page is backfilled. Static output includes semantic Event JSON-LD and aggregate capacity only. The page is composed of @catch/web-ui parts: media (photo or activity-accent poster), title and host, when/where/price facts, description, hosted moments, the plan, where (Open in Google Maps), good to know (included, what to bring, accessibility, cancellation terms and how to join), going and spots left, the organiser card, the organiser's latest reviews labelled as theirs, and more from the organiser. Every optional section closes when absent. Catch events keep the phone-verified guest entry and its payment recovery; imported events hand off to the official source as a recorded booking click. Public pages never carry dating framing (CAT-247).
Private phone-verified event invitation and checkout. Token exists only in the cleared URL fragment and page memory. Marketing analytics excluded.

The signed-in guest's account (no board; drawn from the system): Plans with passes (getEventTicketCode), Following, Reviews with verified state, Details, per-organiser Messages permissions and Privacy and data, the plans, follows and reviews from listeners on the guest's own rows (guestEventStatuses, organizerFollows, reviews) named from publicOrganizers, and the messages from one manageWebsiteAccount read. Signed out it offers the sign-in sheet (phone code, Google, email link). Private shell: noindex, out of the sitemap, no analytics.

The organiser owner's billing on the web (no board; drawn from the system): the free trial, the plan (ticketing or tools-only) with Catch's prices, and bills with their Razorpay invoice to pay. Buying or cancelling tools-only happens only here (manageOrganizerBillingPlan); the native Host app shows status only (App Store 3.1.3(f)). Reads getOrganizerBillingStatus and manageOrganizerBillingPlan, and listens to hostOrganizerBillViews, for an organiser from the owned-organiser listener (every organiser the signed-in user owns; a bill email's ?organizerId= preselects one). Signed out it offers the phone-code sign-in sheet. Private: noindex, out of the sitemap, no analytics.

A walkthrough booking's manage page, which bookWalkthrough's managePath opens (?booking=wt-…; the confirmation adds the manage token as #t=…, which stays in the fragment). Reads, moves or cancels the booking through manageWalkthroughBooking; without a token the booker confirms the booked number on the phone-code sign-in sheet. Private: noindex, out of the sitemap, no analytics, private shell family start.
Phone-authorized payment/admission history independent of public event listing availability. No marketing analytics or new registration.
Private synthetic workflow invitation; fragment grant, verified contact and explicit start. No marketing analytics.

Catch for weddings (programmes), band for band as the RbWebWeddings board on the system in the nights-out format: the running-order hero, why planners switch, one wedding in six chapters, the team, messages and the family, pricing by headcount, the pilot with the step-1 application card (Continue opens /weddings/apply/), questions and the foot band. Every interface excerpt is illustrative, fictional data. Indexed and in the sitemap now that the application posts to the reviewed intake (joinWaitlist, programme weddings).

The Catch for weddings pilot application (RbWebWeddingsApply): step 1 again when the landing did not hand it over in this tab, step 2, and the sent state. Send posts a phone-only Host application with programme weddings to the reviewed intake (joinWaitlist); it stays noindex like the Host application.

Run and walk clubs: the organiser-type template (hero, pains, a run morning, buyer's checklist, pricing at their size, FAQs, capture). The first page wired end to end: website/src/content/playbook/pages/host/run-clubs.json, noindex until the owner approves it.
Padel, pickleball, tennis and badminton.
Applications, seating and prepayment.
Teams, rounds, live scores and repeat bookings.
Cafes, bars and breweries running their own nights.
Yoga, spin, strength and dance studios and instructors.
Mixers and pub crawls. /host/mixers/ stays a retired redirect, so the page lives here (decision 26).
Workshops and classes.
Communities.
Creators.
Companies and shared spaces.
Treks, rides and outdoor groups.
Courts, clubhouses and sports facilities.
College societies (decision 26 gave it this path).
Attribution links and reporting for brand-run events.

How Catch works (product pages v2): the seven feature groups and Forms, before, on and after the night; every group links to its page. Sections whose feature is not built yet stay in the content, hidden (show-when-live).
Bookings and memberships (product pages v2): ways in, a balanced room, memberships, waitlists, UPI payments and refunds. Approvals that carry over and the try-it tool stay hidden until they ship.
Your page (product pages v2): the organiser page as link-in-bio, the owner view and claiming. Custom domains, the events embed, host pixels and the try-it tool stay hidden until they ship.

Messages and growth (product pages v2): event messages, announcements, follower updates, WhatsApp campaigns, tracked links and guest invite links. Promoter commission, ambassador spend, rewards and the try-it tool stay hidden until they ship.

The room (product pages v2): First Hello, groups that mix by format, Help me say hi and the consent rules. Replaces /product/night/ (301). No dating or matching wording; the try-it tool stays hidden until it ships.

Running the event (product pages v2): the door, the live console, dress rehearsal, attendance and door staff. Replaces /product/door/ (301). The host safety view, the finance role and the try-it tool stay hidden until they ship.
Guest records (product pages v2): one record per guest across events, groups with plain rules, merges, export and privacy. AI import and the try-it tool stay hidden until they ship.

Forms (product pages v2), the supporting page linked from the host footer's Resources column: kinds of form, templates, responses and form fees. Importing a form from a link stays hidden until it ships.

Reports and payouts (product pages v2): the event report, payouts into the host's own Razorpay account and the monthly bill. Team roles moved to Running the event; the feedback summary and the try-it tool stay hidden until they ship.
Pricing off the /host/#pricing anchor so it can rank and take ads. A one-off board: its PR adds the sections it needs.
Host verification, Booked on Catch reviews, the code of conduct and reporting.
Who runs Catch and why. Waits on founder content (decision 22).

Where Get notified goes until the guest app ships: the homepage's app launch notice (appLaunchNotice custom section, joinWaitlist notice appLaunch). Indexed (owner, 19 Nov 2026); linked from the guest header action and Explore footer link. Becomes Get the app once the stores are live.
Start free trial, menu-free: store badges, a QR code on desktop and WhatsApp me the link.

Book a walkthrough, menu-free: the slot picker (features/walkthroughs) books an open India-time slot with getWalkthroughSlots and bookWalkthrough after a phone-code sign-in, and links the booking's manage page (walkthrough_manage); when no slot is open, booking is closed or the slots cannot be read, the request form stands below it (decision 24; D8 in #2304).
A public, self-serve demo night. /demo/:invitationId/ stays the private demo (decision 26).
Plan your first event: a plan, a run sheet and what to charge.
Leave the WhatsApp group behind: import, what changes and what does not.
Offsites, retreats and birthdays that are not weddings.
Host-to-host and guest-to-host referral.

Host stories. Built and shelved (content/playbook/pages/resources/index.ts shelvedResourcesPlaybookPages): not served, noindex, out of both sitemaps, linked from nowhere, and its stories band does not render until content/stories/hostStories.ts has real stories (decision 20). docs/marketing_website_architecture.md says how to switch it on.
Comparisons, status quo first. A one-off board.

The no-show calculator (noShowCalculator custom section, features/marketing/NoShowCalculator.tsx): the host's own numbers only, no rate or benchmark of its own. Indexed (owner, 19 Nov 2026); linked from the host footer's Resources column.

The event tool on its own page: a split band whose tool form runs event.import-from-link (features/tryIt, the tool Bookings and memberships uses) and makes a private draft event (name, date, start time, city) the host finishes in the Host app. Indexed; linked from the host footer's Resources column.
The host playbooks hub: the intro and a tile per guide. Indexed (owner, 19 Nov 2026); linked from the host footer's Resources column.
A first-event plan by format and city, such as run-club-mumbai. One content file per plan.

One host story per content file. No story page exists until a real story, with the organiser's written consent, real figures and photos with rights, is published (content/stories/README.md); the template is a Storybook fixture.
One comparison per content file, only against the competitors decision 17 names.
One playbook guide per content file (article section): run-club, supper-club, quiz-night and racket-sports. Indexed (owner, 19 Nov 2026); linked from /playbooks/.
Ad landing pages: always noindex and never in the sitemap, whatever meta.json says.

New to a city, such as /new-to-mumbai/ (PlaybookNewToCity), for every website city: this week's plans in the formats where the host makes the groups from the city's cityPlans read model, or the next two weeks when the week is quiet, the board's authored bands and the WhatsApp capture. Matched before the playbook pages (matchDiscoveryRoute). Indexed, and listed in the Next sitemap for every website city, since the owner approved it (18 Nov 2026). A city that cannot be read renders its unavailable state with a 503.

A city by format, such as /mumbai/run-clubs/ (PlaybookCityFormat): a website city and one of the cityPlans contract's format page slugs, matched before the playbook pages (matchDiscoveryRoute). Indexing and the sitemap follow the read model's formatPages[format].indexing (formatPageIndexingFor: 3+ organisers or 5+ plans, whether or not the city has launched); below the bar the page is the board's thin layout, noindex. A format with no organiser and no plan in the city is a 404; a city that cannot be read, or has no format pages yet, renders its unavailable state with a 503.
